      <description>Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sum når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.
– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

      <title>Flere skadet etter kraftig jordskjelv sentralt i Japan</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flere-skadet-etter-kraftig-jordskjelv-sentralt-i-japan-1.18076688</link>
      <description>Minst 22 personer ble skadet da et jordskjelv med styrke 5,5 rammet Shizuoka-prefekturet i det sentrale Japan. Butikkvinduer ble knust, og folk rømte ut av bygninger.
Ifølge kringkasteren NHK er det ikke fare for tsunamier.
Skjelvet inntraff rundt klokka 1 natt til søndag. Det hadde en dybde på 41 kilometer. Den foreløpige målingen fra Japans meteorologiske institutt, som har ansvaret for overvåking og varsling av jordskjelv, var på 5,7.
Det amerikanske jordskjelvsenteret USGS målte det til 5,5.
I naboprefekturet Aichi ble det målt kraftige rystelser på nivå 5+ på den japanske skalaen – det sterkeste som er registrert der siden 1997.
(NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/eisenkot-far-i-oppdrag-a-danne-regjering-i-israel-1.18076617</link>
      <description>Israels president har gitt opposisjonsleder Gadi Eisenkot i oppdrag å prøve danne regjering.
Hverken partiene som støtter statsminister Benjamin Netanyahu eller partiene som støtter Eisenkot fikk flertall ved valget 27. november.
Netanyahus blokk fikk 53 plasser i Knesset, mens blokken til Eisenkot fikk 48 mandater.
For å få flertall og bli statsminister trenger man 61 plasser i nasjonalforsamlingen. Begge blokkene er avhengig av de 19 mandatene fra de palestinsk-arabiske partiene, mend både Netanyahu og Eisenkot har sagt de ikke vil forhandle med dem.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ruud-fikk-revansje-i-paris-_-klar-for-forste-semifinale-siden-mai-1.18076278</link>
      <description>Casper Ruud har storspilt i Paris denne uken. Nå er han klar for semifinale etter seier over Nuno Borges.
Ruuds oppgjør mot portugiseren endte med 7-6 (7-5), 6-4. De to møttes for bare ni dager siden i Basel, og da snudde Borges kampen til seier.
Ruud og Borges kom til semifinalen proppfulle av selvtillit: Ingen har tapt ett sett på veien, og de hadde heller ikke gitt fra seg mer enn fire game i noen av settene.
Ruud spilte kvartfinale i Paris Masters for andre gang. For Borges, som står med én tittel i karrieren (ATP250), var dette første kvartfinale på Masters- eller Grand Slam-nivå.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/trump_-stephen-miller-blir-ny-stabssjef-1.18076143</link>
      <description>President Donald Trump varsler på Truth Social at hans mangeårige rådgiver Stephen Miller blir ny stabssjef i Det hvite hus.
Han er nå visestabssjef og overtar ansvaret etter Susie Wiles, som skal få en annen rolle i administrasjonene, ifølge Trump.
Miller regnes for å stå bak den kontroversielle innvandringspolitikken til administrasjonen.
Susie Wiles ble USAs første kvinnelige stabssjef da hun ble utnevnt ved starten av Trumps andre presidentperiode.
Før det ledet hun valgkamp-operasjonen og regnes for å ha en stor del av æren for at Trump klarte å bli valgt til president på nytt.</description>

      <title>E6 ved Eidsvoll sperret etter ulykke</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/e6-ved-eidsvoll-sperret-etter-ulykke-1.18076075</link>
      <description>Politiet opplyser at det har vært en front-mot-front-ulykke på E6 like ved Eidsvoll-tunnelen i sørgående løp.
Ulykken skjedde ved kryss nummer 56 Boksrud. En av bilene kjørte nordover i det sørgående løpet, ifølge politiet.
Det satt en person i hver av bilene. En av dem er bekreftet død, den andre er kritisk skadet.
Det var tåke og svært glatt på stedet da ulykken skjedde.
E6 har midlertidig omkjøring i sørgående retning. Omgjøringen går fra kryss nummer 56 Boksrud via FV1551 Trondheimsveien, og deretter ut på E6 sydgående ved Nebbenes, opplyser politiet.</description>

]]>

Dorothy Myo has been named the new commissioner of Indigenous languages, replacing interim commissioner Candice St-Aubin.

Myo, who was raised in Saulteaux First Nation in Saskatchewan, will serve in the role for five years.

Her LinkedIn profile says she is a fluent speaker of Saulteaux, Cree and English and recently worked as the deputy chief of self-government and senior director of policy and research at the Métis Nation-Saskatchewan.

She also led the Saskatchewan Indian Cultural Centre, where she worked to preserve, protect and promote First Nations languages and cultures.

A cabinet decision announcing her appointment says Myo was selected for the role after consultations with Indigenous governments and organizations.

The selection process for a new, permanent commissioner was delayed and St-Aubin’s 90-day term was extended last month.

The term of Ron Ignace, the previous commissioner, ended in July, along with the terms of the office’s directors.

The Canadian Press reported earlier this year an audit is being conducted on the office, which is tasked with helping to preserve at-risk Indigenous languages.

Half a dozen sources, including former employees, told The Canadian Press that over the five years of its existence, the commissioner’s office has failed to move the needle on strengthening Indigenous languages and supporting research.

Instead, they said, the office focused on extensive travel and hosting one big conference in Ottawa that cost $10 million. They also alleged a toxic work environment, bullying and uncompleted projects, and staff quitting in frustration.

The Canadian Press agreed not to name the sources because they feared reprisals.

In a media statement at the time, Ignace said the office has faced challenges but “we succeeded in laying the foundation for an office capable of carrying forward this significant work.”

Canadian Heritage Minister Marc Miller described allegations against the office as serious.

“But part of holding people to account is giving people the benefit of the doubt, and that includes making sure the due process is respected,” he said in June.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 11, 2026.

President Donald Trump said this week that the more than 8-month-old Iran war “militarily is effectively over,” but his administration has kept up the financial warfare in a bid to get Iran to capitulate to U.S. demands over Tehran’s nuclear program.

A magnitude 4.7 earthquake has struck off the coast of Vancouver Island, although there are no reports of damage.

Earthquakes Canada says the quake happened at about 6:45 p.m. Tuesday local time, with the epicentre 10 kilometres beneath the sea floor, about 130 kilometres west of Tofino, B.C.

B.C.’s emergency information system says in a social media post that there were no tsunami threats from the quake.

It was the third and strongest significant seismic event off the B.C. coast this month, after a magnitude 4.3 earthquake near Haida Gwaii on Nov. 3.

A magnitude 4.2 earthquake was recorded about 190 kilometres west of Port Hardy on Nov. 2.

Tuesday’s quakes occurred in the Cascadia subduction zone, an area of intense seismic activity.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 11, 2026.

]]> 1360651 Most of Vancouver Island on flood watch Wednesday morning as rainfall continues https://cheknews.ca/most-of-vancouver-island-on-flood-watch-wednesday-morning-as-rainfall-continues-1360639/ Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:22:31 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360639

Relentless heavy rainfall has triggered a flood watch across most of Vancouver Island and a high streamflow advisory for the South Island.

Shortly after midnight on Wednesday, Nov. 11, the Ministry of Water, Lands and Natural Resources’ BC River Forecast Centre issued an update with a flood watch for the North, Western, Central Inland and Eastern parts of Vancouver Island.

“Rainfall rates through the region were very high last night,” says the forecast centre, adding that since Tuesday, areas of Vancouver Island saw 50-150 mm of rain, with 30-120 mm across the South Coast. Another 40-100 mm of rain is expected Wednesday through West and Central Vancouver Island, says the centre.

The cumulative rain comes after a series of atmospheric rivers last week. The next storm system began drenching B.C.’s coast Tuesday with more heavy rain expected over the next couple of days.

READ PREVIOUS: Orange alert weather warning issued for parts of Vancouver Island

The flood watch is also in place for the South Coast (including Howe Sound, North Shore Mountains, Sea-to-Sky and Central Coast, including Kingcome and Fraser Valley-North, and there is a red-coloured flood warning for the Lower Fraser area.

It adds that the heaviest rainfall is expected to hit west and north Vancouver Island, as well as South Coast areas.

“Temperatures are expected to be warm through Wednesday, with the potential for additional snowmelt from shallow snowpacks in higher terrain of the region,” it adds.

Around 5:30 a.m. Wednesday morning, Environment Canada issued a yellow rainfall warning for North Vancouver Island, particularly in Quatsino, Port Alice and Woss regions, where rainfall could exceed 100 mm.

“An approaching frontal system will bring continue to give heavy rain to the western sections of the region today. After a series of storms that have impacted the region, the ground is saturated, which increases the likelihood of impacts,” says Environment Canada.

Meanwhile, an orange-coloured heavy rainfall warning is in place for West and Inland Vancouver Island, where rainfall could exceed 250 mm from Wednesday through Thursday morning. Storm watchers in the Tofino and Ucluelet areas are being advised to be cautious.

“A very robust frontal system continues impacting Vancouver Island. Heavy rain, with hourly rates up to 10 to 15 mm, will persist through this afternoon. Precipitation rates will ease tonight but periods of rain will continue through Thursday,” Environment Canada said for West and Inland Vancouver Island.

Another weather system is expected to hit parts of the Island Friday, with the potential for localized flooding and possible landslides.

Environment Canada is warning people in these areas to stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts.

The cumulative rainfall across Tuesday and Wednesday could also see rising levels in larger rivers and lake inflows for Sproat and Somass River, says the BC River Forecast Centre

Though eastern parts of Vancouver Island are expected to see less rain, the centre says “high tides and storm surge may increase flood vulnerability near the mouths of rivers on eastern Vancouver Island, particularly on Wednesday,” states the update.

The BC River Forecast Centre is warning people in these areas to avoid river banks with swift- moving water.

“Heavy rain and high streamflow bring increased risk for unstable banks, river erosion, submerged roads, swift water hazards, flooding and landslides. Stay clear of the banks of swift Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship running rivers and never drive across flooded roads, bridges or river crossings.

Meanwhile, a high streamflow advisory is in place for South Vancouver Island, with the potential for “moderate to heavy rain to spillover into watersheds in southern areas,” says the centre. From Wednesday through Thursday, some 40 to 120 milimetres of rain is expected at Lake Cowichan and 30 to 60 mm at Duncan.

“Rivers are expected to rapidly rise through Tuesday and Wednesday, with peak flow forecast Wednesday or into Thursday morning,” it adds.

“At this time of year leaves can clog storm drains and impact urban drainage. Keep storm drains clear.”

BC River Forecast Centre levels explained
  1. High streamflow advisories (yellow): River levels are rising or expected to rise rapidly, but that no major flooding is expected. Minor flooding in low-lying areas is possible.
  2. Flood watch (orange): River levels are rising and will approach or may exceed bankfull. Flooding of areas adjacent to affected rivers may occur.
  3. Flood warning (red): River levels have exceeded bankfull or will exceed bankfull imminently, and that flooding of areas adjacent to the rivers affected will result.

Learn more by visiting the BC River Forecast Centre. Follow the latest weather updates at Environment Canada.

]]> 1360639 Iconic Thetis Lake sign restored after more than 40 years https://cheknews.ca/iconic-thetis-lake-sign-restored-after-more-than-40-years-1360638/ Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:15:00 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360638

]]>

An iconic carved log sign that has welcomed visitors to Thetis Lake Regional Park for more than four decades has been given a new lease on life.

The Capital Regional District (CRD) announced Tuesday that extensive repairs to the landmark are complete, preserving a piece of local history dating back to 1984.

The sign was originally hand-carved on site by Peter Martineau when the park was owned and operated by the City of Victoria. It became part of the regional parks system when the CRD acquired the park in 1993.

After more than 40 years exposed to the elements, the sign had suffered extensive rot, weathering and insect damage, putting its future at risk.

While replacing the sign was considered, strong community support for preserving the original carving prompted the CRD to pursue restoration instead.

Over the past several weeks, regional parks staff removed rotting wood, sandblasted the log and inserted borate rods to help prevent further decay and insect damage. Fresh coats of paint were also applied, and the upper portion of the sign, which was not part of the original carving, was recreated and reinstalled.

On Tuesday, CRD staff and leadership celebrated the completed restoration with a small unveiling attended by Martineau’s children.

“We would like to express our deep gratitude to the CRD for their huge efforts to restore this local landmark that was hand-carved on site in the 1980s by our late father,” the family said in a statement.

“We were touched by the outpouring of community sentiment and support to keep the Thetis Lake sign and we’re so happy this iconic piece will live on.”

The CRD says the repairs are expected to extend the sign’s lifespan, although ongoing maintenance will be necessary as the aging wooden structure continues to face year-round exposure to the elements.

Canadians across the country will pause at 11 a.m. to reflect on the sacrifices and service of Canadian Armed Forces members to mark Remembrance Day.

This year is the 25th anniversary of the start of the Afghanistan war in which 40,000 Canadians served and 159 lost their lives.

This year’s ceremonies also take place just weeks after the tragic fire at Canadian Armed Forces Base Wainwright. Four soldiers were killed and dozens were injured when a wildfire suddenly overtook a training exercise.

All times are listed in Eastern Standard Time.

9:20 a.m. — Prime Minister Mark Carney issues a Remembrance Day message saying “rights and freedoms do not defend themselves” in an increasingly “dangerous and divided world.”

He says today is about honouring those who stepped up to serve their country through the generations. He reads the names of the victims of the Wainwright fire: Sgt. Morgan Wong, Pte. Shaun Farrell, Pte. Aidan Goulding, and Pte. Hayden Lykkemark.

“With their bright futures still before them, they chose to safeguard ours. We mourn their loss, stand with those recovering from their injuries, and hold their families and fellow service members in our thoughts,” Carney said.

—

9:10 a.m. — A Remembrance Day procession has arrived at the National War Memorial in Newfoundland and Labrador’s capital city. Hundreds of people have gathered at the monument in St. John’s, despite the rain. The hushed crowd is preparing for two minutes of silence.

—

8:30 a.m. — People begin to gather along the fence line at the national Remembrance Day ceremony in Ottawa.

—

8:15 a.m. — Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour releases a Remembrance Day message calling on all Canadians to reflect on the courage and dedication of Canada Armed Forces members and the sacrifices made by their families and communities.

She says the Wainwright fire is a reminder that everyone who serves is a human being who “accepts risk on behalf of others and is supported by loved ones who share in the sacrifices that service often demands.”

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 11, 2026

Tofino, B.C. – Stories of war veterans passed were shared over a community meal hosted by Nuu-chah-nulth artist Elizabeth George and the Tofino Arts Council (TAC) on November 8, or National Indigenous Veterans Day. 

The special gathering took place below the Tofino Legion and also featured a display of beaded poppies alongside a photo exhibit titled ‘Remembering Nuu-chah-nulth Veterans’. 

George had two grandpas in the military. Chief Earl Maquinna George left Ahousaht when he was 16 to enlist in the Canadian Army and Reginald “Rusty” Wilson, a member of the Lummi tribe and Cape Mudge Nation, was part of the 101st Screaming Eagles Airborne Division of the U.S. Army. 

“We all stand behind my grandpas,” said George. 

George’s brother Hayupiinulth (Bill George) said Rusty made headlines when he turned 80 for skydiving. 

“It was on his bucket list. It’s the only thing he wanted to do was jump out of a plane,” said Hayupiinulth. 

READ MORE: Remembrance Day 2026: CHEK to broadcast, livestream Victoria ceremony

Rusty was born in Campbell River, B.C. on April 26, 1927, and passed away peacefully on Feb. 27, 2015. He was one of 13 children, he was a residential school survivor, and he attended the University of British Columbia.

In 1951 Rusty joined the U.S. Army and served during the Korean War. 

The Korean War started on June 25, 1950, when North Korean troops invaded South Korea, according to Veterans Affairs Canada. United Nations forces soon joined the fighting, which would rage until an armistice was signed on July 27, 1953. More than 26,000 Canadians served on land, at sea and in the air during this bitter conflict. Sadly, 516 Canadians died. Long seen as a forgotten war, Veterans Affairs Canada says the Korean War is now recognized as an important chapter in Canada’s military history.

In 1998, a cairn was placed on Radar Hill in Pacific Rim National Park Reserve and Tla-o-qui-aht First Nations traditional territory, dedicated to the battle of Kapyong and its importance as a turning point in the Korean War. At the same time, to reinforce Canada’s enduring bond with South Korea, Pacific Rim National Park Reserve was proudly twinned with Hallyo Haesang Sea National Park in Korea.

Code Talkers and Telegraph Lines

George shared that First Nations made great soldiers because they were “good hunters and sharp shooters.” 

According to Indigenous Affairs Canada, many of these Indigenous soldiers become successful snipers (military sharpshooters) and reconnaissance scouts (men who stealthily gathered information on enemy positions).

“They would drop the (Indigenous men) behind enemy lines to set a parameter,” said Hayupiinulth.

During the First World War, Indigenous soldiers also took on the role of code talkers, translating sensitive radio messages into Cree so they could not be understood if they were intercepted by the enemy, according to Indigenous Affairs Canada. Another Cree-speaking code talker would then translate the received messages back into English. 

U.S. forces used code talkers during World War One and World War Two as well. The U.S. Marine Corps operated the largest code-talking program, according to the National Museum of the American Indian, sending about 420 Navajo language speakers to battle. The 2002 film ‘Windtalkers’ tells the story of a marine who is assigned to protect a Navajo code talker.  

“It’s ironic they used (Indigenous) language for coding because they wouldn’t let us use our language,” said George. 

Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ (Ucluelet First Nation) members and Hitacu residents Donna and Larry Jack attended the community meal. Hitacu is Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ’s main village located across the inlet from the municipality of Ucluelet.

Donna shared that you can still see old telegraph lines while walking forest trails between Hitacu and the neighbouring territory of Toquaht Nation.

Telegraph lines were built in the early 1900s and were used for relaying news of emergencies. Using wire and electricity, the telegraph worked by turning electrical pulses into dots and dashes that represented letters of the alphabet. This form of communication was called Morse Code.

“The line to Ucluelet ran along Alberni Canal to Uchucklesaht and up to Silver Lake, overland to Effingham Inlet, then overhead across the inlet, overland again to Pipestem Inlet, and along the shore from Toquart to Ucluelet. From there, it carried on along Wreck Bay and Long Beach to Tofino, connecting to Stubbs Island by underwater cable. This Alberni–west coast connection was completed in 1902. By 1914, it extended from Clayoquot all the way to Nootka,” writes historian and author Shirley Martin in her book ‘Calm Harbour, Turbulent Seas: A History of Ucluelet’.

At the end of the community meal, door prizes were awarded and Dredin Amos, 20, won a Patagonia jacket donated by Redd Fish Restoration Society, which he gave to his girlfriend. 

When asked about his thoughts on modern-day war and the prospect of fighting for his country, he said: “I would want to defend Canada.” 

The ‘Remembering Nuu-chah-nulth Veterans’ photo exhibit is running until Nov. 19. On Nov. 20, the TAC Hallway Gallery will feature artwork by Ucluelet Secondary School students.

While the Island has some well-known tourism hot spots, like Tofino and Victoria, Travel + Leisure recommended travelling up the east coast to make the most out of your dollar.

“Magnificent provincial parks, like Englishman River Falls and Elk Falls, offer free entry for hiking and chasing waterfalls.”

It also pointed to some renowned accommodations, like the Tigh-Na-Mara Seaside Resort in Parksville, which was named one of the top 100 spas in North America by another travel website, Spas of America, earlier this year.

A Nanaimo Cafe and Bakery is going cashless after two recent break-ins and thefts.

The owner says the thefts represent a significant loss and so he’s had to make the difficult decision to remove cash to hopefully deter anyone from breaking into his bakery again.

The Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery in Nanaimo’s Old City Quarter has new signs by its front door and on its till, telling customers it’s no longer accepting cash.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“I think it’s a real shame and it’s happening so often and I think it’s a shame that businesses have to resort to that measure,” said Tammy Bennett, a customer.

The first break-in happened Sept. 6 when two thieves gained access to the building and stole the safe and cash float. Just over a month later on Oct. 10, a thief broke in again. The second time, the thief time to wrench the safe from the wall and stole what was now a different, larger safe. He took it and the cash float again. This time, with cameras in a different location, the video images are better and the bakery’s owner says he recognized him.

“As soon as I saw him the second time on the camera because same outfit and same person looking like the same person as the first one,” said John Akin, owner of the Misty Pines Cafe & Bakery.

Based on the video surveillance, police arrested a suspect later that same day; it turns out he was wanted on an outstanding warrant. After spending hours in jail, he was released the next morning on a promise to appear in court.

“It is upsetting. It’s hard to be a small business,” said Akin. “I think the main problem is the justice system currently in Canada.”

Akin says the bakery had roughly $6,000 stolen in the two break-ins, an amount he calls significant.

Even though 10 per cent of the bakery’s purchases are in cash, he says it makes the most sense to no longer use it.

“Sometimes people miscalculate, like all the time I see shortages on the cash, cash outs like it brings more trouble,” said Akin.

Alberto Castillo was supporting the bakery today after his wife saw the social media post about the thefts and the decision to go cashless.

“It sucks. Obviously, everything is going digital now and now usually everyone has their stuff on their phone, but I still prefer cash sometimes,” said Castillo.

The suspect, who can’t be named, as he hasn’t been formally charged yet, is facing charges of break and enter, theft under $5,000 and possession of stolen property related to the second theft at the bakery, with a first court date set for Dec. 15.

Last year a business owner in the same area as the bakery decided to no longer keep cash in her store overnight after a break-in and theft.
